title: North Carolina's 14th Congressional District Election, 2026
description: North Carolina's 14th Congressional District will hold a general election on November 3, 2026, to elect a U.S. Representative. The district covers portions of Mecklenburg, Gaston, Cleveland, Burke, Rutherford, and Polk counties, including part of Charlotte. Incumbent Republican Rep. Tim Moore faces Democratic nominee LaKesha Womack in a race set against North Carolina's newly redrawn congressional map adopted in October 2025. The district leans Republican — Cook Political Report rates it as R+15 — making Moore the clear favorite, though Womack is running on a platform of economic justice, affordability, and expanded access to healthcare and education.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the NC-14 2026 general election matchup. The Cook Political Report rates the district as Solid Republican (R+15).

candidates.name: Tim Moore
candidates.summary: Tim Moore is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 14th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously served as Speaker of the North Carolina House of Representatives for a decade (2015–2024), where he championed infrastructure development, education reform, and job creation. Moore serves on the House Committees on Financial Services and the Budget, and his campaign focuses on lowering energy costs, expanding homeownership, and cutting wasteful spending.

candidates.name: LaKesha Womack
candidates.summary: LaKesha Womack is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 14th Congressional District, having won the March 3, 2026 primary with 52.2% of the vote. She is a strategic consultant and community advocate who founded Womack Consulting Group, a firm that has spent more than 20 years helping small businesses, nonprofits, and faith-based organizations. Womack also serves as Chief Strategy Officer for ASPIRE Community Capital, a Community Development Financial Institution, and is pursuing a Master of Legal Studies at Vanderbilt Law School. Her campaign platform focuses on affordability, economic opportunity, and access to healthcare and education for working families.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polls exist for the NC-14 general election matchup, so the forecast is based entirely on structural indicators. The district is rated R+15 by Cook Political Report (Solid Republican) under a newly redrawn map adopted in October 2025. Incumbent Rep. Tim Moore brings a strong political profile — former decade-long Speaker of the North Carolina House — and the advantages of incumbency. Democratic nominee LaKesha Womack won a competitive primary (52.2%) but faces an uphill race in a district with a substantial Republican lean. Without district-specific polling, the Republican advantage is clear but confidence is tempered by the absence of survey data.
